pages.title: How it works
pages.text: The apiary simulates a Productive Bees hive without placing bee entities. Each bee slot checks its own matching flower or pollen and writes products to the output area and fluid tank. One idle bee never blocks the others.

pages.title: Tiers and slots
pages.text: The basic apiary has 3 bee slots and two output pages of 9 slots each (18 total). Basic/Advanced/Elite/Ultimate factories have 5/10/15/20 bee slots and also use two output pages. Optional addons register even higher tiers.

pages.title: Reading the picture
pages.text: The red cage input accepts empty/filled cages and resource bee spawn eggs; the blue slot is cage output. Gene treats have a separate slot below the fluid tank. Right-click a middle bee slot with a spawn egg or cage to insert or remove a bee. The output area below has two pages.

pages.title: Shift-right-click insertion
pages.text: Hold a resource bee spawn egg or a filled cage and $(bold)Shift-right-click the apiary$() to insert the bee. A selected empty slot takes priority, otherwise the first empty slot is used. Hold a gene treat to insert it into the dedicated treat slot. Rejected items stay in your hand; a full apiary does not release bees into the world.

pages.title: Bee tooltips
pages.text: Left-clicking a bee slot selects it and highlights the slot. Hovering shows name, age, health, progress, state and nectar; hold Shift to add flower requirement, productivity, endurance, temper, behaviour and weather tolerance.

pages.title: Gene treat feeding
pages.text: Gene sample + honey treat = gene-carrying treat. Feeding can rewrite the matching trait. Two methods: $(li)$(bold)Right-click a bee slot$() with the treat on your cursor to feed that bee; $(li)$(bold)Put it in the dedicated treat slot below the fluid tank$() and let the machine pick.

pages.title: How the machine picks
pages.text: Automatic feeding ranks bees by need: $(li)$(bold)Selected a slot$() (left-click for a highlight) → only that bee is fed; $(li)$(bold)No selection$()→ scan all bees, feed the one with the largest shortfall across the treat's genes. $(br2)Example: insert a treat with Productivity: very high + Weather tolerance: any + Behaviour: metaturnal, and the machine starts with low-productivity, rain-shy, day-only bees.

pages.title: No waste
pages.text: $(li)Trait already matches or beats the treat → $(bold)no consumption$(); $(li)Temper only moves bees $(bold)towards passive$(); $(li)0% purity genes do not count; $(li)Treats carrying a bee type gene can enter the slot but are not automatically fed; $(li)At most one feed per 5 real ticks, with same-tick gating and position phasing.

pages.title: Automating the supply
pages.text: Treats and cages use separate slots. $(bold)Pipes, hoppers and AE2$() can supply gene treats through the machine's item input faces. Pair this with the gene sampler upgrade for a sample → craft → feed loop. The apiary can also restock treats directly from its connected ME network.

pages.title: Exact AE2 restocking
pages.text: Restocking defaults to off for each apiary. Insert a gene treat, then click $(bold)R below the treat slot$(). An online ME network supplies only the $(bold)same item with identical components$(), including gene types, values, purity and custom name. This switch is independent of side configuration A and the centrifuge's I switch.

pages.title: Template and cooldown
pages.text: An empty slot remembers its template; a new treat updates it. Turning R off clears the template but keeps already withdrawn treats. Restocking tries at most once per 5 real ticks, backing off to 200 ticks when stock is missing. A full slot, offline network or exhausted work budget prevents further extraction.

pages.title: Pauses and upgrades
pages.text: Settings, templates and withdrawn treats survive saves, dismantling and upgrades. After resolving an ordinary error, switch R off and on to resume. Unknown extraction/delivery results or damaged saved data remain quarantined and cannot be cleared by toggling. Hover R for the state and check the log for the cause.

pages.title: The two toggles
pages.text: Conversion: once on, convertible items in the feeder are consumed and turned into products; it is off by default, so items act as flowers only and are never eaten. Disable mode: left-click to enter per-slot disable editing (the letter turns orange), then left-click a slot to disable or restore it. Outside the mode, Alt + left-click does the same. Shift-click the toggle to disable or enable all.

pages.title: Feeder stats panel
pages.text: The right panel shows slot usage, Active/Idle, the page number and the inserted flowers; with disabled slots the header becomes "Flowers (N disabled)". The bottom hint line changes with the state, reading either "Items are not consumed" or "Conversion ON: ingredients will be consumed".

pages.title: Factory tiers
pages.text: Each tier upgrades from the previous one and keeps the bees and installed upgrades inside. Do not look at speed alone: the faster combs pile up, the more the centrifuge, chests and network must keep up.

pages.title: Produce every flower source
pages.text: The balance option $(bold)apiaryProduceAllFlowers$() defaults to off and is enabled by Paradox Infinity. Off keeps random single-source production. On produces each distinct valid source currently in the feeder in the same cycle. Empty or disabled slots do not count; duplicate slots and larger stacks add no extra runs. Lumber and quarry bees still obey the duplication blacklist.

pages.title: Dye bees and fluids
pages.text: Each distinct convertible flower produces its dye separately, even when two flowers yield the same dye. Directly supplied dyes are used only when no convertible flowers are available. Every output keeps the existing productivity and upgrade multipliers. Independent fluid production is not multiplied by the number of flower sources.

pages.title: Apiary-only switches
pages.text: On the Items page of side configuration these 14x14 buttons show a green letter when on: A = AE output, M = direct AE output, O = direct container output, D = centrifuge direct link, P = centrifuge priority (full centrifuges buffer inside the apiary and only overflow goes to AE). A/M/P exist only with AE2 installed.

pages.title: When it stalls
pages.text: No progress: check FE, bees and enabled flowers. No output: check output space and the fluid tank. Treat insertion fails: check genes, slot space and matching components. No feeding: check the selected bee, useful traits, purity and bee type genes. No restocking: check R, the template, online network, identical stock and pause tooltip.
